passages.text: To everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven: a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot, a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to break down and a time to build, a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance, a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together, a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing, a time to search and a time to count as lost, a time to keep and a time to discard, a time to tear and a time to mend, a time to be silent and a time to speak, a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.
passages.sermon:
God rules over all things under heaven.
God gives a season for everything.
God appoints a time for every purpose.
There is a time to be born.
There is a time to die.
There is a time to plant.
There is a time to uproot what is planted.
There is a time to kill.
There is a time to heal.
There is a time to break down.
There is a time to build up.
There is a time to weep.
There is a time to laugh.
There is a time to mourn.
There is a time to dance.
There is a time to cast away stones.
There is a time to gather stones together.
There is a time to embrace.
There is a time to refrain from embracing.
There is a time to search.
There is a time to give up as lost.
There is a time to keep.
There is a time to throw away.
There is a time to tear.
There is a time to mend.
There is a time to be silent.
There is a time to speak.
There is a time to love.
There is a time to hate.
There is a time for war.
There is a time for peace.
passages.original: לַכֹּ֖ל זְמָ֑ן וְעֵ֥ת לְכָל־ חֵ֖פֶץ תַּ֥חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃ס עֵ֥ת לָלֶ֖דֶת וְעֵ֣ת לָמ֑וּת עֵ֣ת לָטַ֔עַת וְעֵ֖ת לַעֲק֥וֹר נָטֽוּעַ׃ עֵ֤ת לַהֲרוֹג֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִרְפּ֔וֹא עֵ֥ת לִפְר֖וֹץ וְעֵ֥ת לִבְנֽוֹת׃ עֵ֤ת לִבְכּוֹת֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִשְׂח֔וֹק עֵ֥ת סְפ֖וֹד וְעֵ֥ת רְקֽוֹד׃ עֵ֚ת לְהַשְׁלִ֣יךְ אֲבָנִ֔ים וְעֵ֖ת כְּנ֣וֹס אֲבָנִ֑ים עֵ֣ת לַחֲב֔וֹק וְעֵ֖ת לִרְחֹ֥ק מֵחַבֵּֽק׃ עֵ֤ת לְבַקֵּשׁ֙ וְעֵ֣ת לְאַבֵּ֔ד עֵ֥ת לִשְׁמ֖וֹר וְעֵ֥ת לְהַשְׁלִֽיךְ׃ עֵ֤ת לִקְר֙וֹעַ֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִתְפּ֔וֹר עֵ֥ת לַחֲשׁ֖וֹת וְעֵ֥ת לְדַבֵּֽר׃ עֵ֤ת לֶֽאֱהֹב֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִשְׂנֹ֔א עֵ֥ת מִלְחָמָ֖ה וְעֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם׃ס

passages.text: What does the worker gain from his toil?
passages.sermon:
A worker works hard.
He toils every day.
What does he gain from all his labor?
What profit does he receive from his effort?
passages.original: מַה־ יִּתְרוֹן֙ הָֽעוֹשֶׂ֔ה בַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר ה֥וּא עָמֵֽל׃

passages.text: I have seen the burden that God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them.
passages.sermon: God gives people a burden.\r\nThis burden keeps people busy.\r\nI have seen this burden.
passages.original: רָאִ֣יתִי אֶת־ הָֽעִנְיָ֗ן אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧ן אֱלֹהִ֛ים לִבְנֵ֥י הָאָדָ֖ם לַעֲנ֥וֹת בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the hearts of men, yet they cannot fathom the work that God has done from beginning to end.
passages.sermon:
God made everything.
God made each thing beautiful.
God made each thing beautiful at the right time.
God put eternity in the hearts of people.
People cannot understand all of God's work.
People cannot see everything God has done.
People cannot know God's work from the beginning to the end.
passages.original: אֶת־ הַכֹּ֥ל עָשָׂ֖ה יָפֶ֣ה בְעִתּ֑וֹ גַּ֤ם אֶת־ הָעֹלָם֙ נָתַ֣ן בְּלִבָּ֔ם מִבְּלִ֞י אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹא־ יִמְצָ֣א הָאָדָ֗ם אֶת־ הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים מֵרֹ֥אשׁ וְעַד־ סֽוֹף׃

passages.text: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and do good while they live, and also that every man should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor—this is the gift of God.
passages.sermon:
God gives people life.
God gives people work to do.
I know there is nothing better for people than this.
People should rejoice while they live.
People should do good while they live.
Every person should eat.
Every person should drink.
Every person should find satisfaction in all his labor.
This satisfaction is a gift from God.
passages.original: יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין ט֖וֹב בָּ֑ם כִּ֣י אִם־ לִשְׂמ֔וֹחַ וְלַעֲשׂ֥וֹת ט֖וֹב בְּחַיָּֽיו׃ וְגַ֤ם כָּל־ הָאָדָם֙ שֶׁיֹּאכַ֣ל וְשָׁתָ֔ה וְרָאָ֥ה ט֖וֹב בְּכָל־ עֲמָל֑וֹ מַתַּ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽיא׃

passages.text: I know that everything God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it or taken from it. God does it so that they should fear Him.
passages.sermon:
God acts with eternal power.
Everything God does lasts forever.
No one can add anything to God's work.
No one can take anything away from God's work.
God does this so that people will fear Him.
passages.original: יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּ֠י כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה הָאֱלֹהִים֙ ה֚וּא יִהְיֶ֣ה לְעוֹלָ֔ם עָלָיו֙ אֵ֣ין לְהוֹסִ֔יף וּמִמֶּ֖נּוּ אֵ֣ין לִגְרֹ֑עַ וְהָאֱלֹהִ֣ים עָשָׂ֔ה שֶׁיִּֽרְא֖וּ מִלְּפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: What exists has already been, and what will be has already been, for God will call to account what has passed.
passages.sermon:
God is eternal and unchanging.
Everything that exists now has already existed before.
Everything that will exist in the future has already happened before.
God will call to account everything that has happened in the past.
passages.original: מַה־ שֶּֽׁהָיָה֙ כְּבָ֣ר ה֔וּא וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לִהְי֖וֹת כְּבָ֣ר הָיָ֑ה וְהָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־ נִרְדָּֽף׃

passages.text: Furthermore, I saw under the sun that in the place of judgment there is wickedness, and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.
passages.sermon:
I saw something else under the sun.
I saw the place where people judge others.
I saw wickedness there.
I saw the place where people should do what is right.
I saw wickedness there too.
passages.original: וְע֥וֹד רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ מְק֤וֹם הַמִּשְׁפָּט֙ שָׁ֣מָּה הָרֶ֔שַׁע וּמְק֥וֹם הַצֶּ֖דֶק שָׁ֥מָּה הָרָֽשַׁע׃

passages.text: I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked, since there is a time for every activity and every deed.”
passages.sermon:
God is the judge of all people.
God will judge both the righteous and the wicked.
God sees every person.
God knows every action.
There is a time for every activity.
There is a time for every deed.
God will judge at the right time.
passages.original: אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י אֶת־ הַצַּדִּיק֙ וְאֶת־ הָ֣רָשָׁ֔ע יִשְׁפֹּ֖ט הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּי־ עֵ֣ת לְכָל־ חֵ֔פֶץ וְעַ֥ל כָּל־ הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: I said to myself, “As for the sons of men, God tests them so that they may see for themselves that they are but beasts.”
passages.sermon:
The speaker is Solomon, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
Solomon speaks about all people.
Solomon says in his heart, “God tests people.”
God tests people to show them something.
God wants people to see the truth about themselves.
People are like animals in some ways.
God wants people to see that they are like beasts.
passages.original: אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י עַל־ דִּבְרַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָאָדָ֔ם לְבָרָ֖ם הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְלִרְא֕וֹת שְׁהֶם־ בְּהֵמָ֥ה הֵ֖מָּה לָהֶֽם׃

passages.text: For the fates of both men and beasts are the same: As one dies, so dies the other—they all have the same breath. Man has no advantage over the animals, since everything is futile.
passages.sermon:
Men and animals share the same fate.
Both men and animals die.
Death comes to men.
Death comes to animals.
Both men and animals have the same breath.
Man does not have an advantage over animals.
Everything is futile.
passages.original: כִּי֩ מִקְרֶ֨ה בְֽנֵי־ הָאָדָ֜ם וּמִקְרֶ֣ה הַבְּהֵמָ֗ה וּמִקְרֶ֤ה אֶחָד֙ לָהֶ֔ם כְּמ֥וֹת זֶה֙ כֵּ֣ן מ֣וֹת זֶ֔ה וְר֥וּחַ אֶחָ֖ד לַכֹּ֑ל וּמוֹתַ֨ר הָאָדָ֤ם מִן־ הַבְּהֵמָה֙ אָ֔יִן כִּ֥י הַכֹּ֖ל הָֽבֶל׃

passages.text: All go to one place; all come from dust, and all return to dust.
passages.sermon: All people and all animals go to one place.\r\nGod made every person and every animal from dust.\r\nEvery person and every animal returns to dust.
passages.original: הַכֹּ֥ל הוֹלֵ֖ךְ אֶל־ מָק֣וֹם אֶחָ֑ד הַכֹּל֙ הָיָ֣ה מִן־ הֶֽעָפָ֔ר וְהַכֹּ֖ל שָׁ֥ב אֶל־ הֶעָפָֽר׃

passages.text: Who knows if the spirit of man rises upward and the spirit of the animal descends into the earth?
passages.sermon:
The spirit is the life-force inside a person or an animal.
No one knows what happens to the spirit after death.
No one knows if the spirit of a person goes upward.
No one knows if the spirit of an animal goes down into the earth.
passages.original: מִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ ר֚וּחַ בְּנֵ֣י הָאָדָ֔ם הָעֹלָ֥ה הִ֖יא לְמָ֑עְלָה וְר֙וּחַ֙ הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה הַיֹּרֶ֥דֶת הִ֖יא לְמַ֥טָּה לָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: I have seen that there is nothing better for a man than to enjoy his work, because that is his lot. For who can bring him to see what will come after him?
passages.sermon:
A man lives on earth.
A man works during his life.
I have seen this truth.
Nothing is better for a man than to enjoy his work.
Enjoying work is his portion in life.
No one can show a man what will happen after he is gone.
No one can bring him to see the future after his death.
passages.original: וְרָאִ֗יתִי כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין טוֹב֙ מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׂמַ֤ח הָאָדָם֙ בְּֽמַעֲשָׂ֔יו כִּי־ ה֖וּא חֶלְק֑וֹ כִּ֣י מִ֤י יְבִיאֶ֙נּוּ֙ לִרְא֔וֹת בְּמֶ֖ה שֶׁיִּהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרָֽיו׃
